chapter_theme: The last ten stanzas of Madurai Valaisami's Njanak Kummi, sung to the 'woman of knowledge' as a dance song, compress a Vedantic conclusion: the 'thou' and the 'that' of the great saying are one, the whole world is of one's own nature, moksha is knowledge itself and all other rules are the mind's delusion, egg and body alike become void and beyond them the great void. The thing cannot be told or heard, has no far, and will not stand in word or stone; the song ends by counting its own 185 stanzas and blessing the sadguru's feet and the Tamil of the kummi.
structure_note: The great saying and its names (2693 and 2694); the world as one's own nature and moksha as knowledge (2695 and 2696); what cannot be told, and the void (2697 and 2698); what word and stone cannot hold, and the subtle the guru alone tells (2699 and 2700); the colophon, counting the stanzas and blessing guru, poet and learners (2701 and 2702). The refrains ஞானப்பெண்ணே and கும்மி அடியுங்கடி alternate; the readings give what each stanza adds.

links.note: Both make 'thou art that' a knowing rather than a formula: Tirumular's unwearied knowing of soul and Supreme as one is the saying itself; Valaisami's 'tvam' pada becomes the foot that is the 'tat' pada, and the differences, adjuncts and states are all it.

Kakapusundar's opening makes the sects themselves forms the One shows; Valaisami says one's own sankalpa and vikalpa and the sects all became one's own nature. Both absorb the religions into the One instead of refuting them, which softens the Siddhars' usual attack on samayam.

The Meynjanap Pulambal asks when we shall know the joy a mute who dreamed cannot tell; Valaisami says of the Brahman state that there is neither telling it nor hearing it. Both put the goal outside speech from both sides, speaker and hearer.

Arunagiri's string of negations includes a life that has no distance in space; Valaisami says of the Brahman state that there is no far and no farther. Both deny distance to what is sought, so that seeking cannot be a journey.

Valaisami asserts that egg and body became void and beyond them the great void, and tells the women to dance in delight at a Brahman that 'is and is not'. Kakapusundar's disciple presses the question this leaves open: when all the eggs become void and Brahman alone stands, where are the lives, the siddhas and the Trimurti? The kummi gives no answer.

The void beyond the void: Pattinathar's three voids become void and the first void bare void, with the Lord dancing beyond; Valaisami's egg and body become void and beyond the cutting-off is the great void. In both the series of voids ends not in nothing but in what is beyond them, there a dancer, here the Parapara Brahman.

2693.reading: It became the pada that is 'thou', and in it the foot that is the pada 'that'; the differences, the limiting adjuncts, the states and the many names all became it.
2693.nuance: தொம்பதம் and தற்பதம் are the Tamil forms of the tvam-pada and tat-pada of 'tat tvam asi'; the stanza says the one became the other, with பாதம் (foot) punning on பதம் (word). What 'it' is that became them is carried over from the previous chapter and is the one thing of 2696. The syntax is a chain of nominals, so the reading supplies the subject.

2694.reading: For the sake of a name it is called the peaceful turiya; what is spoken of is self-luminosity; having seen the thing no one can see and become clear within, dance the kummi.
2694.nuance: பேருக்கு, 'for the name's sake', concedes that சாந்த துரியம், the fourth state at peace, is only a label; தற்பிரகாசம், shining of itself, is the Vedantic svaprakasa. The stanza names the state and in the same breath says the naming is a convenience.

2695.reading: Like the Devadatta who gains release, the whole world became of its own nature; Nandi, do not let go; is this not the rule of the grammar?
2695.nuance: தேவதத்தன் is the stock 'Devadatta' of Sanskrit logic and grammar examples, the anyone who serves as the subject of a sentence; the stanza seems to say that, as in the textbook example, whoever is released finds the world to be himself. நந்தியே may address the Lord as Nandi or the guru; விட்டு விடாதே, 'do not let go', then asks him not to release the hold of grace. இலக்கண ஞாயம், the justice or rule of grammar, keeps the textbook figure. The whole stanza turns on this learned joke and the reading is tentative.

2696.reading: This knowledge is moksha itself; every other rule is the mind's delusion; one's own resolving and doubting, and the sects, all became one's own nature.
2696.nuance: ஞானமாம் மோட்சம்: release is not a result of knowledge but is the knowledge. சங்கற்ப விகற்பம், resolve and doubt, is the mind's whole activity in Vedantic terms; adding சமயம் to it puts the religions among the mind's constructs, yet the stanza absorbs them into the one nature rather than condemning them.

2697.reading: There is no far and no farther; there is no telling it and no hearing it; women, look at the Brahman state that none can grant, and leaping, dance the kummi.
2697.nuance: தூரதூரமும் இல்லை, no distance at all, denies that the goal is reached by going anywhere. தாரார் is unclear: 'they will not give', so a state no one can hand over, or a corrupt word; the reading takes the first. The stanza's denial of telling (சொல்வது) stands in a song that goes on telling for 185 stanzas.

2698.reading: The egg and the body both became void, and beyond the cutting-away is the great void; delighting in the Parapara Brahman as what is and is not, dance the kummi.
2698.nuance: அண்டமும் பிண்டமும், cosmos and body, go together as the Siddhars' one system and are voided together. அறுக்கப்பாலும் may be 'beyond what is cut off' or 'even on the side of cutting', that is, beyond the act of negation itself. உண்டு இல்லை, 'is, is not', is the paradox the Vedantic Siddhars use for Brahman; the stanza asks for delight (உவந்து) in it, not for argument.

2699.reading: It will not stand in word or in stone; know and take in hand the Brahma-light, the pure space, the strong silence that shines of itself, O woman of knowledge.
2699.nuance: சொல்லினும் கல்லினும் நில்லாது: neither speech nor inscription holds it, a nod to the song's own limits. சோதிபையாகியை is corrupt or compressed; the reading keeps only 'Brahma-light'. கையரிந்துகொள் is கை அறிந்து கொள், 'know and take in hand', since this text writes அறிந்து as அரிந்து (so also 2701). தூவெளி, the pure space, is Tirumular's word.

2700.reading: In the earth-element purity came under sway, and in return differences arose many and many; the guru will tell the end of the sruti; can the wide subtle be known, O woman of knowledge?
2700.nuance: The first line is obscure: பிருதிவியில் தூய்மை வயமாச்சே may say that the pure one came under the sway of earth, the grossest element, and that from this the many differences (பேதம்) arose, a Vedantic account of the one becoming many in matter. The second half makes the guru, not the sruti, the one who tells its end, and leaves the subtle (சூட்சம்) as a question.

2701.reading: Worshipping the feet of the great ones who have come to know, and not departing from the Tamil of the kummi, the poet says he has spoken a hundred and eighty-five stanzas; long live the sadguru's feet.
2701.nuance: நூற்றெண்பத்தைந்து கண்ணி, 185 stanzas, matches the count of the work as parsed (this unit is the 184th and the next the 185th), so the colophon's count is intact. அரிந்துகொண்ட is அறிந்துகொண்ட, 'who have known'. கும்மித் தமிழ் claims the dance song as a vehicle of knowledge, as Tirumular claims Tamil for the agama.

2702.reading: Long live the sadguru's feet greatly; long live Valaisami's Tamil daily; long live greatly the path of knowledge of those who learn the virtuous Tamil of the Njanak Kummi.
2702.nuance: The poet names himself, Valaisami, and blesses his own Tamil alongside the guru's feet; the வாழி formula is the conventional close of a Tamil work. ஞானநெறி, the path of knowledge, is what the learners gain, not the stanzas themselves.

source_issues: This text writes அறிந்து as அரிந்து (2699 கையரிந்துகொள், 2701 அரிந்துகொண்ட).
2699: சோதிபையாகியை is corrupt or compressed and is not rendered beyond 'Brahma-light'.
2694: அகக்தெளிந்து has a stray letter for அகந்தெளிந்து.
